- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply lagged smoothing: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, model tends to overcorrect; adjust forecast toward historical mean (65–68) for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); cap first 5 days’ forecast at 10% below 30-day true mean.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.00) triggers model to lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
